criteria.criterion: (1) Grouped-CV gain over v3 at matched EXE FPR, clearly outside noise
criteria.evidence: compare_v3_v41.json (produced by compare_v3_v4.py --v4-tag v41 --attack-share 0.5): v3 recipe TPR 0.5746 at 0.941% EXE FPR vs v41 recipe 0.7023 at 0.990% (+12.8 pts); TPR at matched held-out 1% EXE FPR 0.623 vs 0.735 (+11.2). Ablations: rf swap alone 0.686 (+11.1), attack-aware ft alone 0.627 (+5.3). The v41-recipe number equals fusion_v41.json cv_estimate (0.7023354037267082), confirming compare used the same folds/seeds as the trainer. My reproduction (rows.py): the goodware/malware row sets are identical between the v4-era and v4.1 compare runs (5,801 goodware, 1,445 EXE, 1,030 goodware2-dev EXE; 349 malware), 0 dev-pool rows are silently dropped by the 'sha in r4g' filter, and the 5-pt move of the v3 recipe between runs (0.625 -> 0.575) is the fold change (train_v4.py switched fg to norm_group at 15:53 on Oct 18, after the 15:19 compare run); the paired gain is +12.8/+12.9 under both fold assignments. Paired noise check without the f member: (e, rf_v41) - (e, rf_adv) = +13.1 pts (sd 4.9, min +1.4, 50/50 folds; matched-FPR +12.7, 50/50); using a single fold forest instead of the mean of 5 gives +13.9, so fold-averaging does not inflate r4. Grid selection: the 4 pre-declared configs scored 0.710-0.718, within 1 pt, so selection on the dev pool is negligible. Caveats: the gain is the holdout-FPR effect seen from the TPR side (rf_adv scores r>0.5 on 44.8% of goodware2-dev EXE and 31.8% of old corpus+local EXE vs rf_v41 OOF 9.8%/8.0%; the threshold is set by goodware2-dev EXEs, new-EXE FPR 1.27-1.32% vs old-EXE 0.23% for both); malware is family-in-sample for both r members; I did not re-run the LightGBM fine-tunes to get full-recipe per-fold paired statistics for v4.1 (the v4-era family-cluster bootstrap was [+7.8, +18.3]).

Integrity verifier: all 9 pre-registered checks PASS for rf_v41 and ember_ft_v41 with every row count reproduced from code without training (rf_v41 12,800 live goodware; folds 350/340/356/316/376 held groups; fusion fit set 349/5,801/1,445 == fusion_v41.json; 0 sealed-holdout/excluded/eval rows or hashes in any training set; 0 grading-set sha256 anywhere; 0 Sysinternals rows; OOF sets exactly equal the fold groups; recent_test ∩ recent_train = 0; r-only fusion refit from the rf_v41 OOF files reproduces fusion_v41.json to 6 decimals; donors reproduced; 5,819 variants map to originals with matching fold). The rf_v4 leak (140 unfiltered recent_train goodware rows, 25 holdout hashes) is confirmed fixed (0/0). Two residual concerns that do not reverse this: (a) the exported ember_ft_v41 trained on all 1,455 malware plus their attack variants, so the robustness suite is in-sample for v4.1 on the 4 trained mechanisms (bias toward v4.1, which still fails criterion 4); (b) 30 live files also sit in EMBER-2018 train (1 in the fusion fit set; negligible). The eval list still carries 7 alias products (16 files) that v3's ember_ft trained on, which favours v3, not v4.1.

criteria.criterion: (3) Sealed-holdout goodware FPR not worse than v3; EXE FPR not above ~1.5%
criteria.evidence: Recomputed from dataset/work/exp/v41_goodware2_holdout.jsonl and v3_goodware2_holdout.jsonl (291 products, 591 files, 465 EXE, 13 EXE Microsoft-trusted in both): v4.1 EXE FP 2/465 = 0.43% (Wilson 95% 0.12-1.55%) vs v3 43/465 = 9.25% (6.94-12.22%); v4 3/465. All-file FPR 2/591 = 0.34% vs 45/591 = 7.61%. Paired: 41 v3-only FPs, 0 v4.1-only, 2 shared; exact McNemar p = 9.1e-13. Both residual v4.1 FPs are unsigned low-margin ML decisions (PCem_Setup.exe r=0.996 with e=0.0035; TinySnake.x32.exe 3,584 bytes). The rate passes the bar; note the Wilson upper bound 1.55% sits just above 1.5% with n=465, and the holdout has now been read for two candidate comparisons (v4 and v4.1) and must not be used to select a v4.2 threshold.

criteria.criterion: (4) No robustness regression > 5 pts on any attack (deployed thresholds)
criteria.evidence: Deltas recomputed from robustness_v41.json vs robustness_v3.json (n=349, recent_test minus NFS duplicates, serving path, deployed thresholds): clean 0.745 vs 0.877 (-13.2); overlay_64k 0.765 vs 0.903 (-13.8); overlay_1m 0.756 vs 0.854 (-9.7); overlay_4m 0.682 vs 0.802 (-12.0); strings_10k 0.728 vs 0.811 (-8.3); section_inject 0.742 vs 0.862 (-12.0); header_copy 0.797 vs 0.920 (-12.3); cert_blob 0.725 vs 0.891 (-16.6). Every attack violates the 5-pt rule; robustness verifier: bootstrap 95% CI upper bounds <= -4.9 pts, McNemar p <= 4.9e-6, v3-only vs v4.1-only detections 35-60 vs 0-6. Also below the rejected v4: clean -8.6, overlay_64k -8.3, header_copy -8.9, cert_blob -11.2, section_inject -3.7 (p <= 0.007). The suite is biased toward v4.1 (ember_ft_v41 trained on these 349 files and their overlay_1m/4m/strings/section variants) and v4.1 still loses; held-out mechanisms (overlay_64k, header_copy, cert_blob) are its worst (mean -14.2 vs v3), with conditional evasion on header_copy 0.058 vs 0.016 and cert_blob 0.073 vs 0.020. Root cause is the operating point: fusion_v41 OOF fit TPR 0.682 vs v3 0.828, mean clean margin 3.02 vs 4.96, threshold set on 1,445 EXE incl. 1,030 goodware2-dev vs v3's 432 EXE. Diagnostic only: at matched holdout FPR (3/465) v4.1 beats v3 on every attack by +13.5 to +23.8; my trade-off curve (tradeoff.py): v4.1 needs 10/465 = 2.15% holdout EXE FP to reach v3's deployed 306/349 clean detections, and at 7/465 (1.51%) reaches 292/349 vs v4's 304/349 at the same budget.

criteria.criterion: (5) Container gates on arm64 and amd64: build <= 300 s, ready <= 25 s, replies <= 5 s, no benign overruns
criteria.evidence: Container verifier (scratch build context with rf_v41/ember_ft_v41/fusion_v41, --read-only --network none --cpus=1 -m 1g, uid 10001, /model threshold 4.276044044708822 == fusion_v41.json, 51 unit tests OK): build --no-cache 42.4 s arm64 / 28.6 s amd64; ready 3.6 s arm64, 5.4-6.3 s amd64 once the image is unpacked (23.6 s on the very first amd64 run including ~15 s of one-time foreign-image unpack; server itself ready in 8.9 s); no reply > 5 s; OOMKilled=false in every pre-registered run. Native arm64: 13/13 benign files answered 0, max 2.545 s (66.8 MB), memory.peak 896.6 MiB. Emulated amd64 (Rosetta, pessimistic): cold pass had ONE benign overrun (Winhance 64.5 MB, 4.082 s server-side, answered 1) and Git at 4.014 s; warm pass max 3.744 s with 0 FP; memory.peak 973/941 MiB of 1024. So the literal 'no benign overruns' clause was violated once under emulation only; native is clean and the frozen v3 image on the identical emulated gate is strictly worse (4 overrun FPs, one 5.33 s reply, memory.peak 8 KB below the limit with 97 reclaim events), so this is a shared serving-path property that v4.1 improves. Residual risks shared with v3: >60 MB benign files on a slow x86 CPU, and two concurrent large requests OOM-kill the emulated amd64 container. Course-set files are small (max 196 ms on the host). Latency numbers from eval_v3.py/eval_robustness.py (8-worker pools under host load 30-75) were disregarded for this criterion.

methodology_flaws: Criterion 4 compares operating points, not detectors: v3's threshold was set at 0.75% EXE FPR on a fit set with only 432 EXE goodware (fusion.json fit_set), which turns out to be ~9.25% on new unsigned EXEs, whereas v4.1's was set by the same rule on 1,445 EXE including 1,030 goodware2-dev EXEs. Same rule, different goodware, so 'deployed thresholds' means v3 runs ~2.1 fused-logit units looser. The pre-registered rule was kept deliberately (V4_STATUS.md next-step 3) and it is what ships, so it still binds; but it means a v4.x can only pass criterion 4 by also choosing a laxer, pre-registered target, which then collides with criterion 3 (v4.1 needs 2.15% holdout EXE FPR to match v3's clean count).

The robustness suite is in-sample and biased toward v4.1: train_v41.py fits the exported ember_ft_v41 on np.ones over all 1,455 malware plus all 5,819 attack variants, and eval_robustness.py scores recent_test minus dups (349), so 349/349 suite files and their overlay_1m/overlay_4m/strings_10k/section_inject variants are training rows for the f member. v3/v4 share the clean-file overlap only. No robustness_v41 number on those four mechanisms is a transfer measurement, and the 'no regression > 5 pts' comparison is tilted toward v4.1; it still lost by 8-12 pts on them. The gate must be rebuilt with fold models or an ember_ft refit without recent_test.

No clean-ft control was run: the pre-declared grid (v41_grid.sh) varied variant share x rounds (CV 0.710-0.718, within noise) but never ran --no-attack under the same folds and rf OOF, so the clean-TPR cost of attack-aware fine-tuning is unmeasured. Indirect evidence the cost is real: grid with rf_v4 OOF 0.718 vs fusion_v4 0.754 (fold confound), serving path v4 290/349 vs v4.1 260/349 at deployed thresholds, and v4 dominating v4.1 at every holdout-FP budget on the trade-off curve (e.g. 304 vs 292 at 7/465, 288 vs 274 at 3/465).

The dev-pool 'TPR at matched EXE FPR' is the holdout FPR reduction seen from the TPR side, not an independent confirmation (prior-review FLAW 1 still holds): the threshold is set by goodware2-dev EXEs (71% of fit-set EXE), and in my (e,r) replica old corpus+local EXE FPR is 0.23% for both recipes while new-EXE FPR 1.27-1.32% determines the cut. The gain is 'v4.1 no longer flags goodware2-style EXEs', not better malware scoring.

'v3 recipe' in compare_v3_v4.py is not deployed v3: its fusion and threshold are refit on the v4 dev pool, so 0.575 must not be quoted as v3's TPR (deployed v3 is 87.7% in-sample at 9.25% holdout EXE FPR). Also, the v3-recipe number moved 5 pts (0.625 -> 0.575) between the two compare runs on identical rows purely from the fold assignment, so absolute CV TPRs carry roughly +/-5 pts of fold noise even though paired gains are stable; compare_v3_v4.json has no _config and predates the norm_group fold change, so only compare_v3_v41.json is the v4.1 comparison.

Malware is family-in-sample for both r members (recent_train/recent_test is a temporal split within 38 families; rf_adv used --extra-train recent_train and rf_v41 includes the 1,021 recent_train malware), and the f members are family-grouped; every TPR here is 'later samples of known families'. Phorpiex, 40 of the 50 grading malware per project notes, is not among the 38 families (NanoCore is), so none of the dev-pool TPRs predicts grading TPR; the only grading evidence is v3's 48/50 with misses at 3.27/3.07 vs 4.11.

The r4 malware OOF score is the mean of 5 fold forests (500 trees) while goodware OOF and the deployed model are single forests; checked and not a flaw (single-fold substitution gives +13.9 vs +13.1 pts; per-file fold std 0.024). Fusion CV folds are row-stratified, not product-grouped, and the matched-FPR column uses an oracle quantile on the test fold (~3 FPs); both symmetric, noise only.

The sealed holdout has now been read for two candidates (v4 on Oct 18, v4.1 on Oct 19) and the v4.1 recipe was designed after seeing v4's holdout numbers; a third use to pick a v4.2 threshold would make it a tuning set. V4_STATUS next-step 1 (drop the alias-contaminated products from the eval list) was not applied; 7 alias products (16 files, 12 EXE) remain, which favours v3, not v4.1.

Latency in eval_v3.py and eval_robustness.py was measured with 8-process pools on a host at load average 30-75 from concurrent agent jobs (4 v4.1 holdout files > 4 s vs 1 for v3); a drift-free ABBA paired timing gives a v4.1/v3 ratio of 1.015 and both model shapes are near-identical, so only the container gate is valid evidence for criterion 5.

Both v4.1 holdout FPs and all 43 v3 FPs are unsigned EXEs decided by ML fusion; the 12 'tampered_signature' malware catches are threshold-independent for all versions, so the ML layer alone detects 248/337 (v4.1) vs 294/337 (v3) on the clean suite, which is the number that moves under any threshold change.
honest_claims: CAN be claimed about v4.1 vs v3: (a) On product-disjoint, unsigned third-party EXE goodware from the GitHub-releases/Chocolatey distribution, v4.1 cuts the false-positive rate from 9.25% (43/465) to 0.43% (2/465), paired on identical files (McNemar p = 9.1e-13), with no leakage (9/9 integrity checks reproduced from code). (b) On identical dev-pool rows, folds and threshold rule, the v4.1 recipe gives +12.8 pts TPR (0.575 -> 0.702) at ~1% EXE FPR on 349 recent malware, unanimous across paired folds in an (e,r) replica and consistent (+12.9) under a different fold assignment; the gain is the FPR reduction expressed as TPR at a fixed FPR, and ~11 pts of it is the rf_v41 swap. (c) At matched FPR (diagnostic, oracle offsets) v4.1's attacked TPR exceeds v3's on every attack (+13.5 to +23.8 pts at 3/465), and attack-aware training reduced relative fragility on the four trained mechanisms (drop from own clean TPR -1.8 vs v3 -4.4). (d) The v4.1 container passes every hard gate on both platforms and has more latency and memory headroom than v3 on 60+ MB files. CANNOT be claimed: (a) that v4.1 catches more malware as it would ship: at deployed thresholds it catches fewer under every attack and under none (clean 260 vs 306 of 349, -13.2 pts; attacks -8.3 to -16.6), with the suite biased in v4.1's favour. (b) Robustness transfer: the three held-out mechanisms are v4.1's worst (mean -14.2 vs v3) and its conditional evasion on header_copy/cert_blob is 2-4x v3's. (c) That v4.1 improves on the rejected v4: it is 8-11 pts worse at deployed thresholds on clean/overlay_64k/header_copy/cert_blob and v4 dominates it at every holdout-FP budget on the clean trade-off. (d) That attack-aware fine-tuning is free: no clean-ft control under identical folds was run. (e) Holdout EXE FPR proven below 1.5% (Wilson upper bound 1.55%, n=465). (f) Anything measured about the course grading set: it was never accessed. By project notes its 50 goodware are Microsoft-signed Sysinternals tools that the trust layer clears for both versions, and 40 of 50 malware are Phorpiex, outside our 38 training families, so dev-pool TPRs do not transfer; what is known is that v3 met 48/50 with two misses at 3.27/3.07 vs threshold 4.11, and v4.1 is 10-15 pts more conservative at its deployed threshold (OOF fit TPR 0.682 vs 0.828), which is a risk with no offsetting FPR benefit on that set. (g) Absolute serving-path TPRs (87.7% v3, 74.5% v4.1) are in-sample for both ember_ft members and recent_train-family-in-sample for both rf members; only the deltas and the grouped-CV estimates are meaningful.

v4.1 regressed further than the NO-SHIP v4 at deployed thresholds: clean -8.6, overlay_64k -8.3, header_copy -8.9, cert_blob -11.2, section_inject -3.7 (all p <= 0.007); only overlay_1m/overlay_4m/strings_10k are statistically tied with v4.

Transfer to held-out mechanisms is NOT shown: held-out mechanisms (overlay_64k, header_copy, cert_blob) lose more vs v3 (mean -14.2) than trained ones (mean -10.5), v4.1's conditional evasion on them is 2-3.6x v3's (header_copy 0.058 vs 0.016, cert_blob 0.073 vs 0.020), and cert_blob now lowers TPR below clean (-2.0) where v3 gained (+1.4). The attack-aware ft only reduces RELATIVE fragility on the 4 mechanisms it trained on (drop-from-clean -1.8 vs v3 -4.4), and those numbers are doubly optimistic because ember_ft_v41 saw attack variants of these same 349 malware.

Root cause is the operating point: fused clean margin 3.02 vs v3 4.96; fusion_v41 OOF fit TPR 0.682 (v3 0.828, v4 0.736), efr threshold 4.276 with weaker member weights (r 0.808 vs 1.179); sealed-holdout EXE FPR 2/465 (0.43%) vs v3 43/465 (9.25%). The fusion refit traded ~13 pts of clean TPR for ~9 pts of EXE FPR; with 12 tampered-signature catches fixed, the ML layer detects 248/337 vs v3 294/337.

Diagnostic only, not a substitute for the rule: at matched holdout EXE FPR (3/465) v4.1 exceeds v3 on every attack by +13.5 to +23.8 pts and exceeds v4 on the four trained mechanisms by +3.2 to +8.3; this shows the loss is an operating-point choice rather than a worse detector, but as deployed v4.1 catches fewer malware than v3 under every attack and under none.

Absolute TPRs are optimistic for all three variants because both ember_ft members (and ember_ft_v41's attack variants) trained on these 349 malware; only the deltas are meaningful. The suite's v2_tpr column (applies v2 coefficients to each variant's own RF) and max-latency column (8 workers, load avg 50-75 from concurrent agent jobs) were ignored as instructed.
